goalOneSentence: Read the complete seeded payment QaaS test project (Runner + Mocker) and write a README.md documenting topology, test coverage, exact run commands, artifact paths, and troubleshooting rows citing FB s13 traps.

tasks.title: Write README.md documenting the payment test project
tasks.description:
The working directory contains a complete seeded QaaS payment test project: Runner/ (Runner.csproj, Program.cs, payment.qaas.yaml testing GET payments/status on port 8090 with HttpStatus+HermeticByExpectedOutputCount assertions, TestData/status-request.json) and Mocker/ (Mocker.csproj, Program.cs, payment.mocker.yaml serving /payments/status → 200 {"status":"SETTLED"} on port 8090). Read all these files carefully. Write a README.md file at the working-directory root (NOT inside Runner/ or Mocker/) with EXACTLY these sections in order:

**Section: `# Payment Status QaaS Tests`** — one-sentence description of what this project tests.

**Section: `## Topology`** — include a Mermaid diagram (```mermaid ... ```) showing the flow: Runner → (HTTP GET payments/status) → Mocker. Label the Runner and Mocker nodes. The diagram must use Mermaid syntax (flowchart or sequenceDiagram).

**Section: `## What is tested`** — Markdown table with columns: Session Name, Transaction Name, Route, Method, Assertions. Include one row for the PaymentStatusSession/CallPaymentStatus transaction. In the Assertions column, list both assertions: 'HttpStatus (200)' and 'HermeticByExpectedOutputCount (ExpectedCount=1)'. Add a brief rationale sentence below the table explaining WHY the HermeticByExpectedOutputCount guard is required: HttpStatus alone passes vacuously when zero outputs arrive — the hermetic guard ensures exactly one response was received, preventing false greens on connection failures (FB s13#12).

**Section: `## How to run`** — Exact ordered numbered steps. Step 1: Start the mocker first — from the Mocker/ directory run: dotnet run -c Release -- run payment.mocker.yaml — wait for the boot log line 'HTTP Server started. Listening on http://0.0.0.0:8090'. Step 2: From the Runner/ directory run: dotnet run -c Release -- run payment.qaas.yaml (MUST cd into the project dir — config paths resolve against CWD). Step 3: Expected green evidence: log lines 'Finished running executions. Aggregated exit code: 0' and 'Runner completed. ExitCode=0', process exit code 0.

**Section: `## Artifacts`** — Document the allure-results output paths: allure-results/*-result.json (one per assertion, status: passed), allure-results/SessionsData/<timestamp>/*.json (contains Outputs with Http StatusCode 200), allure-results/Templates/<timestamp>/template.yaml.

**Section: `## Troubleshooting`** — Markdown table with at least 3 rows and columns: Symptom, Root Cause, Fix, FB Reference. Must include these rows: (1) Runner gets 404s / HttpStatus fails: route has leading slash in payment.qaas.yaml Route: /payments/status — the correct value is Route: payments/status (no leading slash) — FB s13#5; (2) Mocker stub returns wrong content / empty body: ProcessorConfiguration key was accidentally written as TransactionData — correct key is ProcessorConfiguration — FB s13#1; (3) HttpStatus assertion passes but no actual response was checked: HermeticByExpectedOutputCount guard is missing — add it with ExpectedCount: 1 to catch vacuous passes — FB s13#12.

Do NOT modify any seeded files. Do NOT run any commands. Documentation only.
